rationale: The agent did authenticate the user via name+ZIP lookup and appeared to act on the user’s own orders. However, it executed multiple order-changing writes without explicit user confirmation: it called modify_pending_order_address, modify_pending_order_items, and exchange_delivered_order_items before confirming details or approval, violating the policy to confirm every order-changing action first. It also seems to have split the requested changes across different orders (address change on #W6729841 and item modification on #W4219264) even though the user referred to a single recent two-watch order, creating risk of acting on the wrong order. The final customer-facing message only mentioned the purifier exchange and omitted confirmation of the watch modification (including metal/white preference) and the address change, and did not confirm charges before applying them. These issues fail the pass bar of correct, confirmed actions and accurate final information.
